v4l2/stateless: Increase input buffer count

The decoder client was developed with a single OUTPUT buffer.
This works, but is not as performant as multiple buffers. There
is dimishing returns as the buffer count is increased. The larges
benefit is moving from 1 buffer to 2. 4 is choosen here because
it performs slight better.

v4l2/stateless: Use |decoder_| reference buffer count for allocation

Allocating the correct number of reference frames requires
querying the |decoder_|. This is done from
|V4L2StatelessVideoDecoder| instead of adding logic to the
|*Queue|s because the |decoder_| object which holds the
information lives there.

v4l2/stateless: Clear surface references after dequeue

Surfaces hold onto references to other surfaces
while decoding. Once the buffer has been dequeued,
these references are no longer needed.

v4l2/stateless: Move enqueue to surface reference destructor

There are two consumers of a buffer. The |StatelessDecodeSurface|
and the |VideoFrame|. Only when both are done with the buffer
can it be enqueued.

The |VideoFrame| destructor observer can not be the one
to enqueue the buffer because a |VideoFrame| is only constructed
on visible frames. Some codecs have non visible frames that are
used for reference.

The |StatelessDecodeSurface| enqueues on the destructor, but the
|VideoFrame| holds a reference. This prevents the enqueuing of
a buffer until both references are released. In the case of a
non visible frame there is no reference held by the |VideoFrame|
so it can be enqueued once all decoded frame references are
satisfied.
